title: In-situ simulation for rapid response teams in four hospitals: a stepped multi-site mixed methods evaluation
abstract: Objective: to evaluate monthly in-situ simulation for rapid response teams on real-call performance and to explain how teams, ward nurses and families experience it. Design: stepped introduction across four hospitals in random order over 18 months with a qualitative strand. Primary outcome: time from call to first critical intervention in adult ward calls. Results and conclusions will be written after the study.
introduction: In-situ simulation has shortened time to first critical intervention in a multi-site evaluation, but patient outcomes did not change and simulation scores are poor proxies for real calls.
methods: Six three-month periods; hospitals introduced in random order; linear mixed model with period and phase and a small-sample correction; about 3,470 adult ward calls; interviews and debrief observation analysed with the framework method and integrated in joint displays.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present calls by period and hospital, the primary estimate with its interval, secondary and balancing outcomes, delivery and latent safety threats, themes and the joint display.
discussion: The discussion will interpret the primary estimate given four clusters, use the qualitative strand to explain differences between hospitals, and state implications for the authority's programme.
limitations: Four clusters; open delivery; call record timing; the qualitative sample may favour engaged staff.
conclusion: To be written after the study; it will not claim effects on patient outcomes that the design cannot detect.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for stepped-wedge trials for the quantitative strand, with GRAMMS for the mixed methods report
summary: Draft structured for a stepped multi-site mixed methods report with results left empty.
